text:
Priya: Dropping a super-compact OKR & feedback cheatsheet for new managers. Focus: one-line objective templates, quick metric slots, and three micro-feedback formats you can paste in a review.

Zoe: This looks useful. can we add a tiny rule for objectives that involve cross-team dependencies?

Priya: 1-liner rule: always include a dependency tag (2-3 words) and an owner. e.g., `[payments-dep] Owner: Claire`. Keeps calibration fast.

Ken: Show me the one-line templates pls.

Priya: One-line objective templates (pick and fill):
```
- Objective (customer metric): Increase [metric] from [baseline] to [target] to improve [customer outcome]. [dependency tag] Owner: [name]
- Objective (stability): Reduce [error/class] incidents by [X%] to improve reliability for [product area]. [dependency tag] Owner: [name]
- Objective (velocity): Shorten avg cycle time from [baseline] to [target] to accelerate feature delivery. [dependency tag] Owner: [name]
```

Hannah: Love the dependency tag idea. can you add a 1-line KR pattern?

Priya: KR micro-patterns (one-liners):
```
- Metric KR: Increase [metric] by [X] (measured by [dashboard/link]).
- Output KR: Ship [feature/component] to [audience] by [date].
- Quality KR: Keep regression < [Y%] on [test/metric].
```

Zoe: Nice. what about career-oriented goals vs delivery goals? managers always conflate them.

Priya: Add a type tag: `#career` or `#delivery`. Example: `Objective: Build mentorship program to raise onboarding ramp (#career). KR: Run 4 mentor pairings; survey NPS >= 4.0.`

Ken: Now give me the micro-feedback formats you promised.

Priya: Three pasteable micro-feedback formats (short, neutral, action):
```
- Strength + example (1 line): "Strength: consistently delivers reliable infra; e.g., led rollback-free deploy for X." 
- Impact + suggestion (1-2 lines): "Impact: improved onboarding time by 12%. Suggestion: pair with PM to prioritize follow-up metrics."
- Growth ask (manager -> IC) (1 line): "Growth ask: own a cross-team initiative next quarter to level up stakeholder influence."
```

Hannah: Could we have a one-line self-review formula too? my team hates writing paragraphs.

Priya: Self-review 1-liner formula: `Result | Your role | Evidence (metric/link)` e.g., `Cut error rate 0.8pp | Lead author of retry logic | monitoring link + PR#123`

Zoe: Calibration scoring quick card? managers need to standardize.

Priya: Calibration quick card (one line each): `Impact: H/M/L | Certainty: 0-100% | Effort: low/med/high | Dependency: 1-3 word tag` Example: `High | 70% | med | payments-dep`

Ken: Any suggested phrasing for mid-cycle pivots (when KRs need to change)? I always feel awkward moving them.

Priya: Mid-cycle pivot script (2 lines): "We reviewed progress and the context has changed (reason). Proposed change: [short edit to KR]. I recommend we adopt this to maximize customer impact; can we align now?"

people-ops-bot: Reminder: goal submission closes Friday. Attach your one-line objectives to the form: https://internal.redwood/hr/goals.

Hannah: Can we get an example that ties hiring expectations to team OKRs? managers in hiring loop ask this a lot.

Priya: Hiring snippet to include in JD or interview debriefs: `Key deliverable (90 days): Make measurable progress on [OKR objective one-liner]. Expected signals: shipped PRs, stakeholder alignment notes, dashboard link.` Helps interviewers assess fit for the role quickly.

Zoe: This is great 0% more usable than our long doc. copying into onboarding repo.

Priya: Happy to iterate. ping me if you want a variant that uses company OKR IDs instead of free-text tags.
